A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mixture-compression research, renamed from MC-MoE to MC in v2. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Mixtral quantization and pruning experiments, benchmark scores, ablations and efficiency measurements, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds reasoning, coding, long-context retrieval, pruning and deployment results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The PMQ bit-allocation objective, quantization procedure, median-threshold dynamic pruning and significance-aware token protection remain unchanged. The additional experiments and CUDA implementation disclosure do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds actual evaluation on GSM8K mathematical reasoning, HumanEval code generation and Needle-in-a-Haystack long-context retrieval. These substantially extend task coverage beyond the retained language-modeling, standard benchmark and expert-significance evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds token-kurtosis, token-variance and token-mean pruning comparators against ODP. This is a targeted expansion of dynamic-pruning comparisons; the existing uniform-quantization, BSP and Hessian comparators remain. Wanda is discussed but is not newly evaluated directly.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce HumanEval pass@10, retrieval tests across context lengths and needle depths, alternative pruning rules applied to 30% of tokens, and fixed-threshold sweeps. Tables 13–14 add latency testing across batch sizes, input lengths and A100/RTX 3090 configurations. The original calibration and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New appendices test alternative token-importance statistics (A.7), fixed versus calibrated pruning thresholds (A.8), and latency dependence on workload and hardware (A.9). These substantially extend validation of dynamic pruning and deployment efficiency. Earlier bit-allocation, token-protection and significance-weight ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new HumanEval pass@10 metric and token-variance pruning comparator do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original Tables 2–8 and v1 Table 9, now Table 10, retain their values. New Table 9 reports substantial reasoning/code losses: 2.54-bit PMQ scores 37.67 on GSM8K and 29.34 on HumanEval pass@10, versus 58.30 and 59.15 for FP16. Tables 11–14 add pruning and deployment outcomes, including 52 tokens/s on an RTX 3090.

T1.justification: A.9 adds a mathematical operation-count argument comparing token-importance computation, n^2 + n + mn + n log n, with saved expert computation under stated dimension assumptions. The original optimization, pruning and binarization equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly qualifies the 3.8% average accuracy-loss claim as applying to eight commonsense benchmarks. The principal claims about training-free mixture compression, PMQ/ODP, efficiency and comparisons with dense models otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: A.4 adds a substantive applicability limitation concerning larger losses on challenging reasoning and coding tasks, relating these to reasoning demands and pretrained capabilities. A.9 adds explanations of why saved expert computation outweighs token-scoring overhead and how deployment benefits depend on workload. These extend interpretation beyond v1's existing attention-decay explanation.

D1.justification: A.9 newly discloses HQQ-based CUDA kernel adaptations and provides additional deployment hardware and workload information. Existing calibration details, one-bit storage/dequantization instructions and the code-access link remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish when the kernel adaptations were implemented.

R1.justification: V2 updates the MoE examples in Section 2 to include DeepSeek-R1 and removes the GPT-4 reference. It adds benchmark and quantization-behavior literature supporting A.4, and expands discussion of static versus dynamic pruning in A.7. The central research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the method name to MC, adjusts the title and author information, adds acknowledgments and conference headers, trims some explanatory prose, and inserts appendix sections and cross-references. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the four-panel retrieval visualization in Figure 9 and five substantive result tables: Tables 9 and 11–14. Figure 3 gains explanatory annotations, and some captions and table highlighting change. The original bit-allocation visualization is retained as Figure 10, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence about challenging tasks and deployment variability. Table 9 and A.4 expose important reasoning/code weaknesses, while Tables 11–14 strengthen pruning and efficiency evaluation. This makes the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff and applicability substantially clearer. New evaluation details remain incomplete, uncertainty is still unreported, and hardware configurations differ across timing comparisons, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger empirical assessment.
